ratings.comment: I'm taking the summer semester of databases and the workload is insane. He really needs to adjust it to account for how much time students need. He listens to feedback, but it feels like the things he has to fix are self explanatory. He's an extremely harsh grader, given that students are expected to teach themselves. I just hope there's a curve.

The sheer workload, Misery. Eventually, you do settle into it, but it's nonstop. Reading and quiz for every session, so 2 per wk, anywhere from 3 to 10 plus pages. 14 midterms, each on 2 readings. 7 projects. The material, Not that bad. Informative readings, nice professor, generally logical, can retake or resubmit everything. Mostly self taught.

Don't get me wrong, this professor is knowledgeable in databases and is willing to help anyone. However, the work load is insane, and his lectures aren't great. 2 readings and take home quizzes a week, one midterm a week, and at least one project every two weeks. It's not an exaggeration on how much work there is. He is also open to change.

Generally just a hard class. His quizzes/midterms are very detail oriented so you really need to know everything, that and there's large amounts of reading on his quizzes 50% of the quiz time is reading. His homework's are optional aside from the reading quizzes but I wish he would re-work his quizzes the means are usually 50-60%.

Changed class structure/grading this semester so better than past ratings. Weekly in-class quizzes on Canvas in place of midterms, final exam is a retake of all past summative quizzes. 2 take-home online quizzes a week. HW not mandatory. 7 projects bi-weekly throughout sem. Kinda monotonous lecture but very kind professor available in office hours
DO NOT take this professor! He doesn't teach anything yet forces exams EVERY. SINGLE. WEEK - sometimes TWO 10-minute exams back-to-back in one day! Exam averages are

This class is work heavy. If you need to take the class for your pathway I suggest surrounding it around less work heavy classes or 12 units to be able to be proactive with the class. He does offer great resources to learn the concepts even though it is very overwhelming. I also appreciate his compassion.
you're bound to fail/ score a C, save your gpa and sanity. BS grading system will set u up for failure

This was the most demanding class I've ever taken. Assignments are long, tests are tough, and the grading feels set up to make you fail. He asks for feedback but never implements it. You'll be working nonstop until the final day with no breaks. Unless you have ZERO responsibilities outside of school, I highly recommend avoiding this class.

i repeat DO NOT take this dude over summer, you will be given 4-5 long coding and diagram projects every single week. You will not have a break to yourself, everyday you'll be contributing 4-5 hours of HW  over summer just to score horribly. He's a really nice guy don't get me wrong but the workload is brutal. Don't take if you want to enjoy summer

DO NOT TAKE unless you want 8-10 hours of homework a week I wish I was joking. He has a good heart but there is just no understanding from him that students don't have 10 hours a week to spare for one class on top of the endless reading and most confusing module layout I've ever experienced. Also at least half the class gets a C terrible grading!
ridiculous grading system. no matter what happens, 50% of the class is guaranteed to receive a C.

Welcome to the most feared class within the CSULB CS Department. This man is a walking database, his initials are literally DB. When you ask him a question there's always latency as his brain sends SQL and waits for a response. Good luck soldier.

Graded off CLOs. To get a B must be in top 50% of class participation, A top 25% of participation and have at least 7 CLOs with 4/4 minimum. 2 quizzes a week that count towards participation and 2 hw assignments a week. Ask questions to get more points. Compete against classmates to get a grade higher than C. Major points inflation from quizzes.

Prof Brown is a rly great guy. He gets some hate on RMP, which I feel is a bit undeserved. Yes, his class is rly hard. But, he is fair, and genuinely cares a lot, unlike most professors. Theres a lot of work which did tire me out, but bro is precious and always wanting to help. If you work hard and ask questions, you'll do great and learn so much.

Really sweet guy, always helps you and always answers on teams. Takes the best grade on each assignment so you can take them again during midterms and finals.
The class is difficult tho. Quiz and homework between every class, semester project. Goes from theoretical to "maths" to design and code. Lots of setup to do some homework.

Brown is very knowledgeable and accessible. He sometimes words things confusingly, but it is very easy to gain clarification, and he will help you if you reach out. His main problem IMO is the amount of homework. You will learn a ton, but it becomes exhausting. Be prepared to teach yourself how to set up environments. Overall, good guy.

While the assignments are hard, it is a very useful skill to have in CS, he is willing to give you or the whole class an extension. He is also changing his grading system so more people are able to pass and is not so heavy on getting a good grade on the assignments. It will be hard but he is understanding and will help all the time.

super cool guy, very caring and lenient with his grading. most of this class is self study, since lectures don't really help imo. if you really really care about databases like that and u not tryna self study, then don't take it. but overall this class is relatively simple, it's not bad. 99% of the time pushes due dates if needed. 1 assignment a wk

Don't take the obvious teachers pet recommendation below unless you want to be miserable for an entire semester. If you are willing to glaze the professor like this weirdo did all year go ahead but it won't be easy and you won't actually learn anything useful for working with databases in a professional setting.

Absolutely do not take this professor, he gives the most unclear assignments that take about 6 hours per week to complete with absolutely minimal instruction. He does not make clear how his new grading system works which left the entire class guessing what their grades would be.

People are rating this professor poorly, because they didn't put in the effort and received the grades they deserved (go cry). By choosing this professor, you'll gain a thorough understanding of databases and all details.There is a lot of homework, but without practice, you won't learn. He prepares you well for exams, and very considerate. GL!

worst teacher ever, if you care about your mental sanity DONT TAKE HIM, listen to all the other reviews. Harsh grader, LOTS of homework, doesnt teach alot of the stuff youll need on the homework and expects you to know alot of the material already even though its very confusing. Again LOTS of very difficult homework even with studying.
worst thing was assignments. didn't understand what he wanted and the rubrics were so confusing. just too much to turn in everyweek
worst professor in csulb

Insane amount of work be prepared to take 5 quizzes a week along with group work homework assignments. His lectures when he does lecture are dull and nothing but himself about Boeing is a complete snoozefest also he takes attendance which is also odd Dont recommend taking him

This guy gives an insane amount of work throughout the semester. His lectures are also pretty much useless, he doesn't really go over things in detail or explain any of the assignments well. He just expects you to read everything on your own and know what you're doing ahead of time. The only positive is that he grades fast and is easy to reach

This prof's lectures are so boring and feel like they go on forever, he often wouldn't teach much because the code wouldn't work and relied on the class too much to teach because you gotta participate in classroom problems. There is like a million hw assignments and he grades harshly, it looks like he's allergic to giving 100%. Tests are HARD.

Long boring lectures. Often times can't get his code to work when demonstrating how to do assignments. Homework is long and tedious with unclear directions and rubric. Be prepared to teach yourself 99% of the course. Insane workload. Nice guy and very accessible outside of class but not so good at teaching.  Avoid at all costs!

Brown is by far the most accessible professor I've ever had. He has additional office hours, responds to emails fast, and is available on Microsoft Teams. The class itself is very difficult as he does pile a lot of projects and readings which often makes the class feel like a 4 unit course. However, he's always open to feedback and extensions.

He is passionate about his work but you will never catch a break from him. Multiple readings along with reading quizzes each week, on top of group projects every two weeks, on top of multiple homework assignments every week. If you have other classes on top of his good luck. This class will take up your life for the whole semester.

Professor Brown is a very caring professor. He cares for his students and is available during office hours and on teams throughout the day. Although he's a nice guy, he wasn't that great at teaching the subject with the tools needed for the course. First time teaching and using Python, didn't know exactly why things worked the way they did.

What doesn't help besides the fact that his lectures are very wordy and he doesn't show many interactive examples and taking his morning class, he says that he is still learning some of the tools that are being utilized in the current semester and is crucial for you to know to pass. Does he expect us to know this stuff quickly?

Do not take this professor at all costs. His teaching style will put you to sleep and you will not learn a thing from his lectures. His quizzes do not correlate with the slides he shows us, for a 3 unit class is asking way too much and is overly critical of the hw. Lots of self study since his instructions are unclear for everything.

Prof. Brown is definitely the most accessible professor in the department. The best way to succeed in his course is to go every day and ask a lot of questions to understand the material. The workload is insane, so keep that in mind when taking him, but the amount you learn is pretty insane as well. Also, the projects are resume ready :D

Absolutely loved his dedication towards students. Gives great feedback for even simple questions and was even accessible for group meetings. You can tell how much he cares about your education in how often he publishes supplementary videos/resources. The class itself has high workload, so be ready to put in outside-class time.

This class was my favorite so far in the computer science department. David Brown is extremely knowledgeable about databases and has great explanations should you get confused. He is very accessible outside of class and is easy to approach. The class has lots of homework, but it all helps with learning the material.

One of the best professors I've had. Knowledgeable, kind, and respectful. Very accessible, either through office hours or online thru MS Teams. This class is tough and VERY workload heavy. Ask lots of questions and get help whenever you can, hes more than happy to help. You will be in good hands, but definitely not a class you can coast thru

This class is a lot of work, but he was willing to drop assignments and a project for the benefit of our learning. He gives good feedback and a rubric for every assignment, so make sure you use that as a reference. He was always available for help and support, so communicate any confusion and needs with him.

He's very accessible outside of lecture and even office hours, going out of his way to schedule appointments with students even when he knows its over the amount required. But, this is only because the workload in this class is insane. He will follow the grading rubric to a T. I think he is unaware that we take other courses too.

Top tier prof. Leaves detailed feedback on almost every assignment (and there's a lot of them). You work in groups of 3-4 for the entire semester on hw and projects. He's also really accessible outside of class and will do everything in his power to answer your questions and help you succeed if you just ask. Textbook's also free.

Amazing. You can tell that Professor Brown is passionate about what he teaches. He has been the most accessible professor I have ever had. Whether you reach out to him via office hours or Piazza, he always provides constructive feedback to help you with homework, projects, etc. If you ever have to take CECS323, take Professor Brown!

One of the best professors from the department by far. Hes always accessible if you need any sort of help, goes above and beyond to make sure everyone succeeds and learns. Gives very detailed feedback that helps you grow and learn from your mistakes. Would highly recommend if given the chance. Keep in mind that these classes are meant to be hard.

Professor Brown is a very nice and caring professor. He will work hard with you to get all you're assignments done. He gives a lot of assignments and his exams are reasonable. Instructions could definitely be more clear sometimes but he will do his best to answer questions. He is a very tough grader so A's are tough but B's are easy.

David Brown is extremely approachable and always willing to help students. He never turns a student down for asking for help, and will go the extra mile to help students understand the material. 323 is not an easy class, and Brown's labs were very difficult sometimes, but he always was willing to help students. Take if you want to learn
Prof David is a wonderful professor. Always ready to help. Although there is heavy load of HW, but overall a great teacher.

Not the best lecturer, but during labs and office hours he's extremely helpful. Attendance is only mandatory for quizzes, so no need to demo labs if you know they work. The two exams are pretty hard and take up 40%, final is 25%. Get one-sided cheat sheet for tests, two-sided for final. Drops 3 quizzes out of 8. HW due every 3 weeks. Awesome guy.

PROS: Knows databases extremely well (worked with them for 30+ years); has that dad-humor; very professional; gives detailed feedback. CONS: Will 100% not give you enough time to finish exams. You'll definitely learn about DB's with him but you better believe you're going to work for that grade.

A wonderful teacher, professional and a master of his craft. Taking Brown is a must for relational databases. Students may find his courses demanding but so what? Welcome to college. You'll find quite a few demanding courses. David Brown is the nicest, most student friendly and accessible professor in the CS department.

Prof Brown is one of the nicest guy you'll meet. He is accessible during office hrs or through email. Not much homework. Quizzes and exams are moderately hard. He drops 3 out 8 quizzes. There are 2 midterms and a final. Cheat sheets allow. 13 labs, most are easy, some are harder. Not an easy A class, but achievable. Overall, he is fair.
David Brown seems like a nice guy but he is the most useless professor. His office hours were always packed because of how crappy he teaches his lectures. Just drop this guy if you get him.

i have had easier 400 level courses . tough homework everyday for two points . grading system is very advanced and you have to do the exact thing he tells you to do else you get 0 . lectures are boring but he very nice friendly and accessible during office hours . midterms are really hard . midterms are entirely different than practice questions .

This class felt like it should have been 5 units. He gives A LOT of homework but he gives very detailed feedback when grading the homework assignments. He is a nice and approachable guy and curves the grades at the very end. The tests are extremely long and he is there to try to help you in office hours too. HW was turned in through BeachBoard.

He is extremely nice! He makes a really good "tutor" during labs and office hours! But man, there was no structure to the lectures! Not everyone has time to read that much before a lecture! I would do a lot of outside reading then end up on youtube looking up concepts that I didn't grasp in lecture. NICE ! Quality Professor.

His gives so many assignments that will help you learn databasr design. His tests are very long and the hardest part of the course besides the term project. If you're willing to work hard in his class, you'll have a strong grasp on SQL and databases.

David Brown is a good professor. His hw goes much more in depth than the lectures and labs from my experience. If you are diligent about reading the textbook before each quiz/exam, you shouldn't have a problem. Lectures can be kind of boring but his jokes are so bad that they are great. He is also very accessible outside of class. Go to his OHs.

Great professor. Tough class. This was professor Brown's first time teaching this course. The material is definitely dense and heavy. A lot of homework and lab assignments. Very difficult midterms and final. This course was only manageable because Brown was of  a lot of assistance and gave good feedback, which is rare in many of these CS courses.

This class is pretty challenging. His lectures are kind of boring. There's a lot of assignments, and he's a tough grader. Brown is really nice and provides really good feedback. He's really helpful in office hours and is accessible via e-mail. The tests are not easy, so make sure to study for them.

Do not miss any homework assignments they play a big part in your semester project later on. Tough in the beginning as he expects some kind of SQL language background. Definitely know how to build a UML before taking this class as the assignments and test are majority based off of that idea.

Be aware of lots of homework. He is a tough grader. I think this class was harder than it is supposed to be because he really wants to see what his students are capable of and how far they can go. I spent most of my time for that class. His feedback is incredible for each student and he is a great guy. He really cares about the class.

David Brown gives really good feedback on homework and projects. No joke. They are detailed. He is also reachable via email, even over the weekends! Don't hesitate to email him your work before it's due. He'll check it! He's very nice. Yes, he's new (and new to teaching), but after a few more semesters I think he'll be one of the better professors.

His lectures are a snooze fest. He mostly just teaches off the slides and tells bad jokes. However, he is very nice and helpful during office hours, and he gives great feedback on your work. You can't ditch because there are assignments given during lab that are due by the end of it. The class isn't curved but exams are open book.

After everyone had done well on the first midterm, he increased the difficulty of the class. In his words..."Everyone doing so well on the test is a failing test in my book", which is a respectable answer. He did an amazing job giving feedback and worked with the students when they had specific questions out of the scope of the class.

New professor, not bad, but not too great either.  Borrowed materials and slides from other professor. Wished he gave more concrete examples since he was picky on grading assignments.  Graded on certain curve which can go above the standard scale which can be bad.  Tests were straight forward except for the multiple choice. I would try someone else
